text:
priya: Heads-up — PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/9123 is ready but blocked on design/arch + security review. It introduces an optional cross-tenant cache read path (behind a feature flag) to reduce cold-starts for shard rebalances. RFC: https://docs.redwood.ai/rfcs/2026-04-cross-tenant-cache.md 

ben: Copy. Quick summary for reviewers: which services touch the new path? ETA for docs update?

priya: Only router-service and cache-proxy. Added perms check and a feature flag + opt-in policy per customer. I updated the PR description with the high-level diagram, will add an appendix to the RFC with threat model. Docs: short note in infra-runbook is drafted.

jeff: Need architecture signoff before merge. Main concerns: 1) surface area of cross-tenant reads (blast radius), 2) fallback behavior if flag misconfigures, 3) SLO delta. Can you paste the SLO impact here?

priya: SLO delta estimate: p50 ~0ms, p95 +3ms, p99 +8-12ms in worst case (cfg dependent). Cost estimate: ~+3% token compute in steady state. Fallback: router reverts to per-tenant cache read and logs a metric 'cache.cross_tenant_fallback' for alerting.

elaine: Security: we'll need a short threat model + explicit list of endpoints and auth checks. Also want a tolerance test proving feature flag cannot be flipped by tenant-scoped credentials. Please add that to the RFC appendix or PR tests. Tagging @jeff for arch.

priya: Will add threat model and an integration test that asserts access denied for tenant-scoped creds. Also adding an ops playbook step to rollback the feature flag.

ben: For rollout propose: 1% traffic for 24h with strict error budget monitoring, then 5% 24h, then 25% etc. Include a canary that runs perf bench every hour. Add automatic fallback if cache.read_error_rate > 0.5% or p99 exceeds baseline +30%.

deploy-bot: CI: all unit/integration checks passed. Perf-regression: perf-test/cache-read-p99 increased from 28ms -> 36ms on one run (investigate).

jeff: OK I can do arch review today evening. Priya — once you add the threat model + canary/runbook notes, ping me and I'll add the approving comment (assuming security is happy). Elaine, can you advise if the integration test is sufficient or do you want an external audit?

elaine: Integration test looks fine for initial rollout. If we go to broad deployment we'll want a short security checklist review (not full audit) and to record KMS/HSM usage for any key material touched.

priya: Thanks — updating RFC appendix and PR now, will ping when done.

jeff: Perfect. Leaving a note here: do not merge until both arch + security explicit approvals are in the thread. :thumbsup:
